_authority: L50 - fast fixes, quality kept (owner, 2026-10-15). fix/GUIDE.md and scripts/fix.py read this file; change a number here and both follow.
_why: GAS ADVANCED, 2026-10-09..12 (FEEDBACK_LOG #61-#93): one module took 1-1.5 h to build and a small fix about 30 min, because every fix went through the build's whole process - a fixer agent per module, each re-measuring every slide at two sizes, then the orchestrator re-checking, then a whole-course QA, then a visual sweep; up to six agents at once until the PC was unusable and the usage limit hit (#71, #76, #85, #90: 'bro it takes too long'). A fix is not a build: it touches a few things, so it checks those things, once.

space.what: slides with free space (a NOTE since 2.116.0 - never a failure)
space._from: GAS ADVANCED QUALITY_BAR: teaching slides ink >= 45 % at 1280 x 800; S9 'space up and down from that is awfully much'
space._sparse: task-start, check, opener and end slides are listed separately - sparer by design, but QUALITY_BAR #4 says they are not empty either

text.what: slides with text too small to read in the room
text._from: QUALITY_BAR #3: every text run >= 16 px at 1280 x 800 (floor.json's 12.5 px is the sign-off minimum, not the course's own)

overflow.what: slides whose content runs off the screen

layout.what: space, text size and overflow together - one measurement gives all three

last-slide.what: every module's last slide, and whether it has the same design as a reference module (--like N)

kind.what: every slide of one kind (--kind Task, Check, Hand-off ...)

words.what: every slide and script screen that says a phrase (--words "...")

checks._rule: After a fix, run ONLY the check for the kind of change - once, by whoever made the fix. No second checker, no orchestrator re-check, no whole-course QA, no second screen size unless the change was about that size. 2.116.0 (operator, 2026-11-09): AFTER ANY FIX the walk review (kind walk) runs on every touched slide - the old 'no visual check after a fix' is gone.

walk.for: ANY fix - every touched slide is walked like a trainee
runs: fit_gate.py --walk-dir at 1280 x 800 on the touched modules
the reviewer (one Sonnet subagent per batch of 3-4 sheets, never whoever made the fix) -> walk_review.py sign --built-by
walk_review.py verify - fails stop the fix; two rounds at most, then the operator accepts what is left on record (walk_review.py accept) or has it fixed (reopen)

words.for: slide or task words, titles, instructor notes changed

layout.for: space, size, position, spacing, fonts, a picture made bigger, CSS
runs: measure_slides.py on the touched modules at 1280 x 800: no overflow, no text under the floor; before -> after for swept slides

package.for: a file added, moved, renamed or linked; a shared file copied into modules

look.for: a new or changed component, animation or interaction

never_in_a_fix: a QA agent after the fixer - the fixer runs the check itself and reports its numbers
re-measuring slides that were not touched
two screen sizes, unless the operator asked about the projector
a contact sheet of slides nobody touched (the walk review covers the touched slides only)
a whole-course QA pass - that is for the build's sign-off and the handover
re-reading the whole factory - fix/GUIDE.md, COURSE_STATE.md and STANDARDS.md are enough
more than 2 agents at once - one session does a scripted fix alone; agents only for hand work in many modules

agents.when: only for hand work (redrawing, re-composing) in more than 3 modules; a scripted change (words, a shared file, a setting) is done by the session itself

standards._why: a course-wide wish the operator said once - 'the last slide like this', 'text bigger', 'all buttons 56 px' - is written down once, numbered, and every new module is built to it, so it is never repaired again (GAS ADVANCED S1-S10 lived only in that course's review folder)

shared._why: a component every module uses (the end-slide recap, the full-screen viewer) is changed once in one place and copied into every module by fix.py sync-shared - each module stays self-contained (L43), and nobody fixes 19 copies by hand
